findings.problem: The reviser kept the baptism dispute as Constantine's floorNote and says in the flags that it is a note 'about faith and doctrine'. It is not. It is a dispute between two sources (Eusebius against the Zachariah chronicle) over where and when he was baptized. It says nothing about whether he stands within the faith the Nicene Creed states. This is the same misuse B4 fixed for Patrick, Justinian, Bede and Grotius. The revision brief says source caveats go in sourcing. As the entry stands, the page shows a floor note that is not a floor judgment, and Constantine has no floor statement at all.
findings.evidence: p2/Draft_r1.json constantine-the-great.floorNote: 'How and when he was baptized is disputed. Eusebius says ... A Syriac chronicle that goes under Zachariah's name says Eusebius is wrong ...'. The flag 'FLOOR NOTES' says it stays 'as floor notes about faith and doctrine'. Release 29 floorNote values in cic-website/data/world-census.json (augustine-of-hippo, simeon-of-beth-arsham, john-calvin) each state the person's standing against the Nicene faith. Person_Revision_Brief.md: 'caveats about dates or sources go in sourcing'.
findings.fix: floorNote: 'Not in question. He called the bishops to the council at Nicaea.' (This scores FRE 81. Its second sentence rests on the existing row 'He called the bishops to Nicaea, says Eusebius'.) Move the two baptism paragraphs, unchanged, to the end of sourcing, and set their six fact rows to field sourcing. If the coordinator thinks the baptism bears on his faith, the floorNote must say how, from a source. Retelling the dispute does not do that.

findings.problem: To keep Reading Ease at 60, the reviser cut 'their edict' and wrote 'Eusebius copies it whole.' Now 'it' has no antecedent, because no sentence in the paragraph names the edict. A reader will take 'it' for 'the religion they chose'. The rest of the departure is accurate. 'In 312 Constantine began to tolerate the church' is R12's own text, and row 74 supports the freedom sentence.
findings.evidence: p2/Draft_r1.json: 'Together they gave Christians and all others the freedom to follow the religion they chose. Eusebius copies it whole.' npnf201 50285-50287: 'to grant both to the Christians and to all men freedom to follow the religion which they choose'.
findings.fix: 'In 312 Constantine began to tolerate the church. Later he and Licinius met at Milan. Their edict gave Christians and all others the freedom to follow the religion they chose. Eusebius copies it whole.' (scored FRE 62.6, FK 6.6). Update row 74's sentence to match.

findings.problem: The rewording goes past Foster in two places. (a) 'It fell on all his fellow Arminians' adds 'all'. Foster says only 'the ban laid upon his fellow-Arminians'. (b) 'He found a kinder welcome among the English ones' leaves 'He' unclear (Foster is the last person named). 'Welcome' also suggests a personal welcome. Foster's 'kinder reception' is about how his ideas were received: the next lines say his works 'were highly prized in England'.

findings.problem: Para 1 now says Macrina kept 'the words of Gregory the Wonder-worker'. That is correct. But row 117 quotes only Letter 204 ('the blessed Gregory'), and its sentence claims 'whom the Library names as Gregory the Wonder-worker' without quoting that naming. Row 118 names him at a different passage (On the Holy Spirit 74). The Library does name him for this passage, in the editor's life of Basil, which points to Ep. 204.
